### 2026-10-11 – ## 10/10 - A lot of new changes; too many one might say

**7.2h**

## 10/10 - A lot of new changes; too many one might say
## just an overview to start:
I wanted to make the starbie more interactive, so I thought of three things to add
- piezo buzzer for sounds
- Light sensor for night/day mode
- vibration motor for haptics (favorite addition imo)

luckily work cancelled my shift today so I have time to do all this.

I. Buzzer

I used a passive piezo buzzer to simulate sound, which was pretty cool as i never did a project with sound before. not muchh to say, i decided to use a PS1240P02BT buzzer which i chose cause it was really cheap and not too obscure.
heres the exact part I found for it that I thought was pretty useful:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Iutzf4NJrsg8BTRXuOaOKBNF3tLaJknK/22a07b4c4c2de82668d54b47c87003862e765ef79fc0527e09f2a629175e0404.png)
It is very "Hot" whatever that means

II. Light

The light sensor was a bit challenging because I added leds in my previous session, so that would kinda make it not work as well. I came up with a couple solutions tho. 1. I could remove the sensor and code a set time where it switches to night/day, but that would remove some of the interactivness. 2. I could turn off the LEDs when the light sensor senses, which I might do later in addition to my chosen solution. 3. Move the light sensor away from the leds. pretty simple and paired with the 2nd solution would be pretty nice.

III. Vibration

I had a lot of issues with this because, like the light sensor, i didnt want it interfering with other parts. I ended up putting it in a different corner of the star than the mpu, so everything should be fine I hope
heres the zoomed in module on the pcb which i was very proud of:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Iutzf4NJrsg8BTRXuOaOKBNF3tLaJknK/23dc5a166d2b3d1a4af7fe4b64390e45a8eb9fdcc177b06da99fc3dad5ac38d7.png)

### Issues:
favorite part lol. because of the very compact design, and trying to fit everything onto the star shape, i ran into issues on two fronts: Wiring and ground pours. The high ammounts of parts used required me to be very efficient with my space, which i think i did. The ground pours was also an issue because the influx of paths all over the place made for seperated islands of ground pours that needed to be connected. There where some easy fixes but a lot of rewiring had to be done to get this monstrosity put together. Unfortunately, I also had to drasticaly decrease the pattern I had cause it now inteferes with the important modules I added. :(

Here is one of the issues i spent 10 minutes looking at before realizing i could just make the wire go the other way
